Name: Riyanshi Verma
Project Description: Technical hiring and interview preparation suffer from critical inefficiencies and structural inequities on both sides of the table: 1. For Job Candidates: Traditional mock interview platforms are flat, text-heavy, and unrepresentative of real engineering panels. Real technical interviews are dynamic, multi-perspective committee discussions where architects probe failure mechanics, product managers evaluate ROI, and leadership checks ownership. Existing practice tools rely on static, turn-based chatbots with polite delays, unable to handle conversational barge-in or interruptions. Furthermore, post-interview feedback in existing tools consists of vague generalities ("improve your communication") rather than quote-indexed receipts linking scores to exact candidate statements. 2. For Hiring Teams and Recruiters: Engineering organizations burn approximately 80% of senior engineering sprint hours conducting repetitive first-round phone screens. Standard automated screening tools provide only text transcripts or generic summaries that lack defensible, auditable hiring signals. Additionally, human interview panels are susceptible to unconscious demographic bias, interview fatigue, and inconsistent rubric application across candidate cohorts. Solving this problem is paramount. Hiring teams urgently require an automated, objective, and defensible evaluation pipeline that screens thousands of applicants without sacrificing senior engineering hours, while candidates from all backgrounds require accessible, high-fidelity interview training calibrated to rigorous enterprise standards. And my solution, Vocalis AI solves this challenge by transforming the interview process from an isolated text prompt into a collaborative, real-time voice committee that evaluates candidates across structured stages and generates audit-grade hiring signals. Key Workflow and Architecture: 1. Dynamic Calibration & Context Ingestion: Candidates or recruiters upload a resume and Job Description/rubric. The system parses technical skills, work history, and notable projects to generate an anchor bank and configures an active 5-persona committee with tailored questioning strategies. 2. Real-Time Voice Streaming via Agora SD-RTN™: Voice communication runs over Agora’s Software Defined Real-time Network using WebRTC Opus audio (48kHz HD). Microphone capture routes to Deepgram Nova-3 speech recognition, achieving sub-100ms latency. Hardware-level Voice Activity Detection (VAD) and acoustic echo cancellation enable natural voice barge-in, allowing candidates to speak over the AI and take the floor instantly. 3. Multi-Agent Backstage Deliberation: After each candidate answer, the multi-role committee deliberates behind the scenes via Groq (Qwen 3.8 27B) and Google Gemini. The engine classifies response depth, detects contradictions or vague buzzwords, updates five competency scores, and decides which panelist takes the floor next with authentic conversational transitions. 4. Precision Stage-Based Progression: Sessions progress through structured stages (Stage 1: Intro, Stage 2: Project Deep Dive, Stage 3: Skills & Edge Cases, Stage 4: Behavioral/HR, Stage 5: Wrap-up & Evaluation) tailored to difficulty tiers (Foundational 15m, Intermediate 25m, Senior/Staff 45m+). The interview concludes cleanly without looping indefinitely, while candidates retain the ability to click "Finish & Evaluate" at any moment for immediate teardown and evaluation. 5. Dual-Workspace Delivery: - For Candidates: Delivers live difficulty sparklines, real-time quality alerts, an interactive system-design whiteboard canvas inspected by the AI, and Turn Time Machine replay capabilities. - For Recruiters: Provides an enterprise talent dashboard featuring cohort demographic tracking, automated rubric import, CSV exports, 360° radar dossiers, and fairness/parity compliance tooling.

Name: Shivansh Sood
Project Description: AI-generated voices from tools like ElevenLabs and OpenAI TTS have gotten so good that you genuinely cannot tell them apart from real people anymore. This is already being used for phone scams, identity fraud, and spreading misinformation. The detectors that exist today are mostly black-box neural networks that just spit out a confidence percentage with no explanation for why they think something is fake, and they break the moment voice cloning models get a little better. We built Voiceprint to solve this differently. Instead of training another AI to guess whether audio is fake, we measure the actual physics of how human voices work and check whether the audio obeys those physical rules. Here is what we look at. When you record audio with a real microphone in a real room, the mic always picks up background thermal noise, room echo, and electronic hum. The silence is never truly silent. But when an AI generates speech, the pauses are literally digital zero, perfect mathematical silence that no physical microphone can ever produce. We measure the near-zero sample ratio inside pause frames and the noise floor depth, and if the quiet parts of a clip are unnaturally clean, we know it was generated, not recorded. We also measure vocal fold micro-tremors. Human vocal cords have physical mass and involuntary muscle tremors that cause tiny pitch and amplitude fluctuations on every single cycle. Synthetic voices are either too smooth or have weird jumps at phoneme boundaries. On top of that, humans have to breathe to speak, so we detect inhalation sounds before speech onsets, something TTS engines never bother to model. And neural vocoders trained on compressed audio cut off high frequencies sharply below 4.5 kHz, while real human consonants like "s" and "sh" push energy well past 5.5 kHz. The key differentiator is that every single verdict comes with transparent evidence. We do not just say "88% likely AI." We show you exactly what we measured: "18.0% near-zero samples in pauses, noise floor at -85 dB, zero breath inhalations detected." You can take those numbers and verify them yourself with any standard audio analysis tool. We tested it against ElevenLabs voice clones, OpenAI TTS, LuvVoice, and multiple real human recordings. 12 out of 12 classified correctly with zero false positives. The whole thing runs on pure CPU with no GPU needed, and analysis takes under 2 seconds per clip.
Feedback: High-impact real-world problem relevance addressing critical user needs; functional repository codebase backed by an accessible live deployment. Next step: expand automated test suites and production containerization.

Name: Kamalesh Ramu S V
Project Description: Problem: The internet has evolved into an active psychological battlefield. Every day, millions of users are manipulated by "dark patterns"—deceptive UI designs meticulously engineered to steal money, harvest credentials, and trick consumers into forced-continuity subscriptions. To combat this, the cybersecurity industry built scanners and threat-detection platforms. But these tools introduced a fatal flaw: The Privacy Paradox. To check if a sensitive checkout page, a banking portal, or a suspicious email link is safe, users are currently forced to copy that URL or take a screenshot and upload it to a third-party cloud server. We are asking users to surrender their browsing habits, private transactions, and sensitive data to a corporate server just to verify their safety. You should not have to pay for security with your privacy. Lumina Security Engine eliminates this compromise entirely. It is a paradigm shift in consumer protection: a 100% offline, privacy-first Progressive Web App (PWA) that acts as a personal, on-device threat sandbox. By pushing the computing power directly to the edge—the user’s own device—Lumina changes how threat detection operates: Zero-Cloud Architecture: Lumina never sends user data to the cloud. By leveraging WebAssembly and in-browser Optical Character Recognition (Tesseract.js), screenshots of sensitive checkouts are analyzed entirely on local memory. The data never leaves the machine. Off-Thread Heuristic Engine: Instead of relying on slow cloud databases that fail against zero-day phishing sites, Lumina actively parses the raw code and text on the device. It hunts for behavioral triggers like artificial urgency ("Account Suspended"), fake countdown timers, hidden subscription clauses, and unverified password fields. Sandboxed Isolation: Users can safely open a malicious link inside Lumina’s strict HTML5 sandboxed iframe. It neutralizes malicious scripts, allowing users to visually inspect a threat without compromising their browser. Radical Accessibility: Security tools are often built for engineers. Lumina is built for everyday consumers. It translates complex DOM analysis into an instant, traffic-light verdict: Safe, Suspicious, or Critical Danger. Solution: Lumina proves that the future of consumer security is local. It shifts the power dynamic back to the user, providing an enterprise-grade, privacy-absolute shield against the deceptive mechanics of the modern web, ensuring that protecting your wallet no longer means exposing your data.

Name: POOJARI NAGASHIVA
Project Description: CipherMind AI ’26 was built to address a practical challenge in cybersecurity: detecting network threats is not enough — security analysts also need to understand why an incident was flagged, how severe it is, and which incidents are related. We developed the system progressively, starting with UNSW-NB15 dataset validation and binary attack detection. We compared Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and CatBoost, with CatBoost achieving the strongest overall performance. We then performed feature-ablation experiments and discovered that TTL-based features could be removed with almost no performance loss, making the final model less dependent on dataset-specific shortcuts. Multiclass attack-family classification was added next, along with uncertainty-aware top-k predictions for attack families that naturally overlap. The pipeline was then extended with unsupervised anomaly detection, evidence fusion, behavioral correlation, SHAP-based explainability, and a local LLM summary layer. The LLM does not make security decisions or access raw network-flow data; it only converts the evidence already produced by the detection pipeline into an analyst-friendly incident summary. The final system therefore moves beyond simple classification toward an explainable SOC assistant that can detect, prioritize, correlate, explain, and summarize suspicious network activity. What I learned Detection accuracy alone is not enough. A cybersecurity system must also provide evidence that analysts can understand and act upon. Feature leakage and dataset shortcuts matter. The id feature showed strong correlation with the label despite having no meaningful security interpretation, while the TTL-family ablation showed that removing suspicious shortcut signals caused almost no performance degradation. Different models have different strengths. CatBoost provided the best overall binary detection performance, while Random Forest offered slightly higher attack recall. Real-world generalization is harder than validation performance. The validation-to-test performance gap showed that strong validation results do not automatically guarantee equally strong performance on shifted data. Some attack families are intrinsically difficult to distinguish. Analysis, Backdoor, and DoS showed substantial behavioral overlap, so forcing every incident into a confidently stated single class can be misleading. Top-k predictions and ambiguity flags provide a more honest representation of uncertainty. Combining multiple sources of evidence is more useful than relying on one model. Supervised probability, anomaly detection, model agreement, SHAP explanations, and behavioral correlation provide complementary perspectives. Explainability should be evidence-based. SHAP helped identify meaningful behavioral signals such as TCP handshake timing, packet characteristics, services, and connection-context features after TTL features were removed. LLMs are better used as a communication layer than as the detector. Using a local Ollama model keeps the system free and allows the LLM to summarize already-computed evidence without replacing the underlying ML models. A good SOC system should prioritize analyst decision-making. The goal is not simply to output “Attack” or “Normal,” but to answer: What happened? Why was it flagged? How confident are we? What incidents are related? And what should the analyst investigate next?

Name: Naveen V Hiremath
Project Description: The Problem: The Spatial Blind Spot in Drug Development Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is the leading cause of late-stage clinical trial failures and post-market drug withdrawals, costing the pharmaceutical industry over $2.6 billion per failed candidate. The root cause of this failure is a fundamental blind spot in our preclinical testing tools: they lack spatial and temporal resolution. Current computational models (like standard PBPK software) treat the liver as a single, "well-mixed" bucket. They can accurately predict the average drug concentration in the organ, but they completely miss the spatial reality of biology. They cannot simulate how reactive metabolites accumulate and cause localized necrosis specifically in Zone 3 (pericentral), nor can they model how chronic, low-dose exposure causes diffuse, grid-wide regeneration failure over months. Because of this "black box" approach, toxic compounds slip into human trials, and safe compounds are prematurely abandoned. The Solution: Digital Liver We are replacing the "well-mixed bucket" assumption with a spatial, mechanistic digital twin. Digital Liver is a preclinical dose-triage prototype that models the liver not as a single compartment, but as a spatial hexagonal lattice of ~768 functional lobules. By simulating the tissue at this micro-architectural level, we can visualize exactly where and how drug-induced injury develops over a 1 to 30-day horizon, catching spatial toxicity patterns that traditional models miss. How It Works: A Two-Tiered Physics Engine The simulation operates on a highly optimized, mechanistic architecture: Macro Scale (Systemic PK): A 1-compartment pharmacokinetic model calculates the plasma drug concentration over time, accurately handling both single bolus doses and repeated 24-hour dosing cycles. Micro Scale (Spatial Lobule Lattice): The liver is modeled as a 24×32 hexagonal grid. Blood perfuses inward from the portal corners (Zone 1) to the central vein (Zone 3). Each hexagonal agent runs its own explicit Euler ODE system tracking the parent drug, reactive metabolites, glutathione (GSH) depletion, and cellular damage. Crucially, the agents feature neighbor-coupling, allowing acute Zone-3 damage to physically spread to adjacent lobules as a localized necrotic wave. Key Innovations Dual-Pathway Injury Modeling: Unlike models that only simulate acute overdose, our engine explicitly differentiates between Acute Toxicity (CYP-saturating, GSH-depleting necrotic waves) and Chronic Degeneration (where a 24-hour moving average of metabolite load silently suppresses cellular repair, leading to grid-wide failure over 30 days). Interactive Spatial Visualization: Researchers watch injury unfold in real-time on an interactive canvas (healthy pink → amber → dark necrotic) and can click any individual lobule to inspect its internal Z1/Z2/Z3 micro-diagnostics. Automated Clinical Triage: The system translates complex spatial data into clear, actionable verdicts (e.g., "SAFE," "TOXIC," "CHRONIC LIVER FAILURE") and exports plain-text triage reports, bridging the gap between computational biology and immediate decision-making. Zero-Backend Execution: Built entirely with React, TypeScript, and HTML5 Canvas, the simulation runs locally in the browser, rendering 30-day horizons interactively in seconds with zero server latency. The Grand Vision: Module 1 of a Full-Body Digital Human The liver does not exist in isolation. Digital Liver is the proven, mechanistic foundation of a planned full-body in silico simulation pipeline. Our roadmap is to sequentially apply this exact spatial lattice architecture to build Module 2: The Digital Kidney (modeling nephron/cortex-medulla gradients), and Module 3: The Digital Heart. Eventually, these deep, validated organ modules will be linked via a shared systemic plasma compartment. Our ultimate goal is to provide pharmaceutical researchers with a comprehensive, whole-body digital environment to test multi-organ crosstalk and systemic trade-offs before a single human trial begins.

Name: Shivansh Gupta
Project Description: India's manufacturing corridors generate tens of millions of tonnes of reusable industrial by-products every week — clean PET scrap, cotton cutting waste, corrugated cardboard offcuts, mild-steel fabrication trimmings — yet most of it ends up in landfills or gets sold at throwaway scrap rates. The problem isn't that recyclers don't exist. It's that no one can find each other, trust each other, or make a justified procurement decision. Existing waste portals are blunt classified boards with no matching intelligence, no quality assurance, and no explainability. CircularMatch is a full-stack, AI-powered industrial symbiosis platform that converts a manufacturing waste stream into a discoverable, evidence-backed secondary raw material — matched deterministically with the most compatible industrial buyers and recyclers. A factory operator types a plain-language waste description. Google Gemini 2.0 Flash extracts material type, quantity, frequency, grade, and location into a structured draft — but is explicitly prohibited from guessing chemical composition or assigning quality grades. The supplier reviews every field, then publishes. The platform then runs a 100-point deterministic matching engine (not an LLM — so results are repeatable and auditable): Material Compatibility (35 pts) + Quality Grade (20 pts) + Quantity Fit (20 pts) + Logistics Radius (15 pts) + Evidence Completeness (10 pts). Hard eligibility gates run first — a buyer is excluded entirely if the generator is outside their haulage radius or below their quality minimum. Every match surfaces a mathematical "Why this match?" breakdown, a net economic calculator (sale revenue minus transport cost plus avoided disposal fee), and a governed environmental impact estimate — all with fully disclosed assumptions. A Digital Material Passport (aligned to ISO 59040:2025) tracks lot codes, packaging, storage conditions, and a 4-tier evidence chain from Supplier-Declared (Not Verified) → Document Uploaded → Platform Reviewed → Test-Reviewed (Lab Certified) — creating the audit trail industrial buyers need for EPR compliance. Real impact in numbers (illustrative Delhi NCR scenario): A Noida injection moulder disposing of 2,600 kg/week of PET scrap pays ₹20,800/week in disposal costs. CircularMatch routes that same clean material to a Manesar recycler at ₹14–17.50/kg — generating ₹30,160/week in net recovered revenue after freight, a swing of ₹50,960/week (~₹26.5 Lakhs/year) for the generator, while the buyer saves 25–35% vs. virgin PET resin and avoids ~3,900 kg CO2e weekly. Stack: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite (Vercel) · FastAPI Python 3.12 + Pydantic v2 (Render) · Supabase PostgreSQL · Google Gemini 2.0 Flash · Leaflet geospatial routing · 7 passing backend test suites. Live Demo: circularmatch.vercel.app Instead of treating industrial waste as a disposal problem, CircularMatch treats it as a discoverable raw-material resource — with the transparency and trust that real industrial procurement demands. LearnLoop then runs a loop: Diagnose: the AI breaks the goal into weighted sub-skills. An adaptive diagnostic finds your real level in each one. Retain: your mastery score decays over time. Missed questions become spaced-repetition flashcards, and there is a review queue, a weekly study plan and daily streaks. Prove: a proof-of-work ledger records what you demonstrated, with a public page you can share. Highlights Live voice loop: speech in, AI reply, speech out, using the browser's speech recognition and an ElevenLabs voice. Coding round: a sandboxed in-browser code runner with AI code review. Study pods: small groups of learners can join with a code and run live peer mock interviews over chat. Time-to-Ready estimate: a forecast of how long until you're job-ready, worked out from your progress. Level-matched resources: learning links chosen for your level. Name: Shravan Khanal C
Project Description: Problem Statement : Mule accounts are used to launder proceeds of cyber-fraud. Money enters through victims, is split, delayed and forwarded across many accounts, and exits through hawala or crypto gateways. Existing systems score accounts and transactions one at a time, so they freeze the disposable mule accounts while the coordinators and recruiters behind them stay hidden. They also flag knowing participants and unwitting victims the same way, and their black-box scores can't be turned into evidence. The gap is network-level visibility with explainable, evidence-ready output. Solution TraceNetX v2.0 is a mule-account intelligence and network-disruption platform. It treats laundering as a network and reconstructs the whole chain from victim to exit. Investigators can follow the money, identify the coordinator, and file action-ready evidence from a single dashboard. Novelty Willing vs. unwitting classification separates knowing participants from likely victims. Layered network map arranges accounts into criminal, recruiter, mule, intermediary and exit layers, so the chain of command is visible. Explainable, evidence-ready output: each flagged account carries SHAP-based reasons, a risk tier, a recommended action and an evidence package for STR filing and agency referral. Combined behavioural, graph and temporal detection in one pipeline, including hawala mapping and crypto-gateway monitoring. Bring-your-own-data: any transaction CSV can be uploaded, and the pipeline retrains and re-flags automatically. Methodology Ingestion: transactions (sender, receiver, amount, timestamp, plus optional IP, city, phone and transfer type) are loaded and enriched with missing attributes. Feature engineering: per-account behavioural features such as outgoing counts, unique senders, IP concentration, average incoming amount and maximum single transfer. ML detection: a supervised ensemble (XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest) combined with an Isolation Forest for unseen anomalies. SHAP explains every score. Graph intelligence: community detection, convergence analysis, hawala mapping and crypto-gateway monitoring, which reveal mule clusters converging on coordinator nodes. Temporal analysis: rule-based sequence detection for dormant reactivation, delayed layering, velocity spikes, smurfing and rapid forwarding. Role classification and response: accounts are assigned roles and risk tiers, then mapped to recommended actions and exportable evidence packages. Validation: nested cross-validation with data-leakage audits, so reported performance reflects generalisation.
Feedback: High-impact real-world problem relevance addressing critical user needs; functional repository codebase backed by an accessible live deployment. Next step: expand automated test suites and production containerization.

Project Description: **Problem Addressed:** Every day, restaurants, wedding halls and canteens have surplus food that is still safe to eat. Much of it is wasted because donors cannot quickly find an available NGO, verify whether the food can reach people before it becomes unsafe, or coordinate pickup on time. Existing approaches mainly connect donors and NGOs, but they do not adequately check time-based food safety or manage failed responses. **Our Solution:** FeedBridge is a WhatsApp-based surplus food rescue system. We validated the need with **five restaurants, four NGOs and five wedding halls in Puducherry**, and also coordinated a real food donation to an NGO. **FeedBridge does not merely find someone who wants the food—it checks whether the food can reach them safely and on time.** WhatsApp prototype screenshots and the working system flow have been included in the PPT.

Name: Srilakshmi S
Project Name: FoodRescue – Smart Surplus Food Management and Redistribution Platform
Project Description: FoodRescue: A Smart Surplus Food Management and Redistribution Platform Every day, restaurants, hotels, colleges and event organizers end up with edible food they cannot use, while NGOs and communities nearby struggle to find enough meals. The problem is not always a lack of food. The people who have it and the people who need it simply do not know about each other at the right time. FoodRescue is a full-stack web application that solves this coordination problem by connecting food providers, NGOs, volunteers and administrators on one platform, so surplus food reaches people instead of the bin. The platform supports four roles, which users choose on the first screen before logging in. Food providers post surplus food with the food type, quantity, pickup location, preparation time and the time until which it stays available. NGOs browse and search the available donations and accept the ones they need. Volunteers accept the pickup, collect the food from the provider and mark it as picked up, then mark it delivered to the NGO. Administrators oversee the entire system. They verify or suspend accounts, view every donation, monitor platform statistics such as total users, donations, deliveries and meals rescued, and export donation reports as CSV. Each donation moves through a controlled lifecycle: available, accepted, collected and delivered, or cancelled or expired. Only the right user can make each change. For example, only the assigned volunteer can mark a pickup as collected or delivered, and two people cannot claim the same donation at once. A donation that nobody accepts before its deadline expires automatically, which supports food safety. Providers, NGOs, volunteers and admins receive in-app notifications at each key step, such as when an NGO accepts a donation or a volunteer is assigned. Dashboards show live figures for each user, including donations made and meals rescued. Security is built into the system. Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes and sessions use JWT tokens. The server checks the role on every request, so users cannot see or change another role's data, and public sign-up cannot create administrator accounts. Login and registration are rate-limited, and all inputs are validated on the server. The application uses Node.js and Express for the backend, MongoDB with Mongoose for the database, and a responsive HTML, CSS and JavaScript frontend. It can be deployed publicly using MongoDB Atlas and Render. Future scope: maps and distance-based matching, food photo upload, automatic matching of donations to the nearest NGO, and surplus prediction using past data
